profile.name: Feather Step
profile.tagline: A forward-moving foxtrot figure with a distinctive outside step and subtle body turn.
profile.insight: The feather step, introduced in 1920, features a unique third step outside the lady with a slight rightward body turn, spawning multiple variations.
profile.profile: The feather step is a dance figure in International Style foxtrot, typically consisting of three or four steps with the man stepping forward. The third step is distinctive, taken outside the lady on her right side with a slight turn of the body to the right. Different syllabi vary on whether a fourth step realigning partners is included. This figure has inspired several variations including curved, overturned, back, and hover feathers, as well as complex endings like the feather finish and feather ending.
profile.profile_long: The feather step is a fundamental figure in the International Style foxtrot, first introduced in 1920 by G. K. Anderson. It generally consists of three or four steps, with the man stepping forward. The hallmark of the figure is the third step, where the man steps outside the lady on her right side, accompanied by a slight turn of the body to the right. This distinctive movement creates a dynamic and elegant line between the partners. The Imperial Society of Teachers of Dancing (ISTD) syllabus includes a fourth step that realigns the man with the lady into a normal dance position as part of the feather step variation, whereas the International Dance Teachers Association (IDTA) syllabus does not include this step. The feather step's unique pattern, especially steps two and three, has led to several variations such as the curved feather, overturned feather, back feather, and hover feather. Additionally, the figure serves as a basis for more complex endings like the feather finish, where the first step is taken backward (known as the continuity finish in American Style), and the feather ending, where the first step is taken in promenade position. These variations and endings expand the expressive possibilities of the foxtrot, making the feather step a versatile and essential element in ballroom dancing.

sections.origins_and_history: The feather step was first introduced in 1920 by G. K. Anderson as a figure in International Style foxtrot. It has since become a staple figure, recognized for its distinctive third step outside the lady and slight rightward body turn.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The feather step consists of three or four steps, with the man stepping forward. The third step is taken outside the lady on her right side, with a slight turn of the body to the right. The ISTD syllabus includes a fourth step to realign partners, while the IDTA syllabus does not. The figure is danced in a smooth, flowing manner typical of foxtrot. sections.notable_figures: G. K. Anderson is credited with introducing the feather step in 1920.
sections.regional_variants: Variations of the feather step include curved feather, overturned feather, back feather, hover feather, feather finish (continuity finish in American Style), and feather ending (first step in promenade position).

Step 4: (ISTD only) Man steps forward with left foot to realign with lady
